sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Interviewers use testing knowledge as a signal for code quality thinking. Can this developer write testable code? Do they know the difference between a mock and a spy? Can they test a React component without testing implementation details? These are the questions that separate job-ready freshers from those who need hand-holding.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
- **Test pyramid**: many unit tests (fast, cheap), fewer integration tests, fewest E2E tests (slow, expensive).
- **Unit test**: tests one class in isolation; all dependencies are mocked.
- **@Mock** creates a mock; **@InjectMocks** creates the class under test with mocks injected.
- **when().thenReturn()** = stub; **verify()** = assert a method was called.
- **@WebMvcTest** = Spring context with only the web layer (controller + filters); no service/repo.
- **React Testing Library**: query by what the user sees (text, role) not by component internals.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- JUnit 5: @Test, @BeforeEach, assertEquals, assertThrows — know these by name.
- Mockito: @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class), @Mock, @InjectMocks, when/thenReturn, verify.
- @MockBean = Spring-managed mock (use in @WebMvcTest/SpringBootTest); @Mock = Mockito-only mock (use in pure unit tests).
- Jest: describe/test/it, expect().toBe(), jest.fn() for mocks, jest.mock() for modules.
- React Testing Library: screen.getByRole/getByText over getByTestId — test behaviour not implementation.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- "What is the difference between a unit test and an integration test?" → Unit test: one class, all deps mocked, no Spring context; integration test: multiple real components working together.
- "What is the difference between @Mock and @MockBean?" → @Mock is pure Mockito; @MockBean registers a mock in the Spring ApplicationContext — needed in @WebMvcTest.
- "How do you test a Spring Boot REST controller?" → @WebMvcTest with MockMvc — loads only the web layer, @MockBean for services.
- "What is the TDD cycle?" → Red (write failing test) → Green (minimum code to pass) → Refactor.
- "Why does React Testing Library prefer getByRole over getByTestId?" → Role queries test what the user experiences; testId tests implementation details.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I write unit tests with JUnit 5 and Mockito. For service classes, I use @Mock to mock repositories and @InjectMocks to create the service, then use when/thenReturn to stub calls and verify to assert interactions. For controller tests, I use @WebMvcTest with MockMvc — it loads only the web layer so tests are fast. On the frontend, I use Jest and React Testing Library, querying by role and text to test what the user sees, not internal component state."*
